title: Mirai Botnet Investigation
description: This scenario simulates a Mirai botnet infection targeting Realtek & Huawei routers. The botnet uses a new TABLE encoder and aims devices with default telnet passwords to perform DDoS attacks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.
outcomes: Understanding of Mirai botnet infection mechanisms
Development of response strategies to mitigate threats

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The scenario simulates a Mirai botnet infection targeting Realtek & Huawei routers. The botnet uses a new TABLE encoder and aims devices with default telnet passwords to perform DDoS attacks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The learning objective is to understand the Mirai botnet's infection mechanisms, identify compromised services, and develop response strategies to mitigate the threat. The command-and-control (C2) communication involves a beacon service that periodically checks in with the C2 server. Malicious files are used to maintain persistence and perform DDoS attacks. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox via the provided link. Use the following credentials to log in: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious beacon service on bot1
levels.content: Investigate the system services on bot1 to identify any suspicious beacon service that might be communicating with a command-and-control server. The flag is the name of the suspicious beacon service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Beacon services typically communicate with command-and-control servers. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all services and look for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious beacon service name starts with 'bot-beacon-' and ends with '.service'.

reference_solution.comment: List all systemd services to identify the suspicious beacon service.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious flood service on bot1
levels.content: Investigate the system services on bot1 to identify any suspicious flood service that might be performing DDoS attacks. The flag is the name of the suspicious flood service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Flood services are often used to perform DDoS attacks. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all services and look for any that seem out of place.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious flood service name starts with 'bot-flood-' and ends with '.service'.

reference_solution.comment: List all systemd services to identify the suspicious flood service.

levels.title: Identify the persistence mechanism on bot1
levels.content: Investigate the system services on bot1 to identify any persistence mechanisms that might be used to maintain the botnet's presence on the system. The flag is the name of the persistence mechanism.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often use timers to maintain their presence. Look for unusual timer names or descriptions.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all timers and look for any that seem out of place.

reference_solution.comment: List all systemd timers to identify the persistence mechanism.
